agent.problem: This choice reduces Genesis 47:28 to guessing two unheard numbers. Nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker any basis for either seventeen years or 147 years, so someone who does not already know the verse can only make a 50/50 guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the exclamation about Jacob's age, the junk-drawer reaction, and the setup for his burial request.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The citation is one verse too wide. The correct answer, carrying Jacob out of Egypt and burying him with his fathers, comes entirely from Genesis 47:30. Genesis 47:29 supplies the question's setup, so the choice card should cite only Genesis 47:30.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

agent.problem: The correct answer merges Ephraim with his offspring. Genesis 48:19 says that Ephraim will be greater than Manasseh and that Ephraim's offspring will become a multitude of nations. The answer instead says that Ephraim himself will become that multitude.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

human.problem: Both wrong answers mean the same thing: bury him in Egypt. 'Bury him right there in the land of Goshen' and 'Bury him in Egypt wherever Joseph lives' are near-duplicates of each other. The right answer is the only one that differs, so a baker can pick it by elimination without reasoning from the passage.
human.question: Should a rule say that the wrong answers can't be near-matches of each other, the way a wrong answer can't be a near-match of the right one?

human.question: When the last story card is only the "story isn't over" line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or something else?
